Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

(Updated at 15:30 hrs NST on 28 August 2026)

August 28, 2026, 05:00 PM

Flash Flood in Bhote Koshi River of Nepal on 26 August 2026

(Updated at 15:30 hrs NST on 28 August 2026)

Severe flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River area of Nepal on 26 August 2026, resulting in huge loss of lives, widespread displacement and extensive damage to houses, roads, bridges, hydropower facilities and other critical infrastructure.

Nepal’s security and disaster-management agencies, local authorities and health services have been fully mobilised for search and rescue, evacuation, emergency medical assistance and relief operations. The river systems and downstream flood risks are being continuously monitored. The Government of Nepal is utilising all resources at its disposal for the search, rescue and relief efforts for all those affected.  

 So far, 538 bodies have been recovered from the river areas, while many people, both locals and tourists, are still missing. According to the latest available information, out of 632 people from 33 countries, 121 have been found and 511 are still missing (list attached). These figures remain subject to verification as search and rescue operations continue.

At this stage, our immediate and utmost priority is to save lives and support search and rescue, evacuation and relief efforts in the affected areas. Contributions for these efforts can be made through the link: https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np/.

In view of the extensive damage caused by the floods to critical infrastructure, the Government will continue to assess the situation and emerging needs on the ground and, where necessary, communicate specific requirements for assistance through established official channels.

Furthermore, over eighteen International and Nepali media were briefed regarding the current status of search, rescue and relief operations of the Government. The briefing also highlighted that Nepali security agencies are currently handling the search and rescue operations effectively, and that international support will be sought as per the necessity in specific areas of expertise, while a more comprehensive assessment will be made for resources required for rehabilitation and reconstruction. It was also highlighted that Nepal was open for international travelers/tourists as only specific part of the country was affected.

Further updates will be available at https://mofa.gov.np/content/1862/notice--emergency-response-team-for-assistance-regarding/.

Emergency Response Team at the Ministry can be contacted at Emergency Hotline/WhatsApp:      98XXXXXXXX, 98XXXXXXXX (7am to 10pm); and Email: emergency@mofa.gov.np.

The nearest Nepali Mission can also be contacted for details and possible assistance.
